title: The Tattooed Men
year_evidence: 扉に『Philippine Folk Tales / Compiled and Annotated by / Mabel Cook Cole / 1916』
text:
_Igorot_

Once there were two young men, very good friends, who were unhappy
because neither of them had been tattooed. [110] They felt that they
were not as beautiful as their friends.

One day they agreed to tattoo each other. One marked the breast and
back of the other, his arms and legs, and even his face. And when he
had finished, he took soot off the bottom of a cooking-pot and rubbed
it into all the marks; and he was tattooed beautifully.

The one who had done the work said to the other:

"Now, my friend, you are very beautiful, and you must tattoo me."

Then the tattooed one scraped a great pile of black soot off the
cooking-pots, and before the other knew what he was about, he had
rubbed it all over him from the top of his head to the bottom of his
feet; and he was very black and greasy. The one who was covered with
soot became very angry and cried:

"Why do you treat me so when I tattooed you so carefully?"

They began to fight, but suddenly the beautifully tattooed one became
a great lizard which ran away and hid in the tall grass, while the
sooty one became a crow and flew away over the village. [111]
paragraphs: Once there were two young men, very good friends, who were unhappy because neither of them had been tattooed. [110] They felt that they were not as beautiful as their friends.

One day they agreed to tattoo each other. One marked the breast and back of the other, his arms and legs, and even his face. And when he had finished, he took soot off the bottom of a cooking-pot and rubbed it into all the marks; and he was tattooed beautifully.
The one who had done the work said to the other:
"Now, my friend, you are very beautiful, and you must tattoo me."

Then the tattooed one scraped a great pile of black soot off the cooking-pots, and before the other knew what he was about, he had rubbed it all over him from the top of his head to the bottom of his feet; and he was very black and greasy. The one who was covered with soot became very angry and cried:
"Why do you treat me so when I tattooed you so carefully?"
They began to fight, but suddenly the beautifully tattooed one became a great lizard which ran away and hid in the tall grass, while the sooty one became a crow and flew away over the village. [111]
あるとき二人の若者がいた。たいそう仲の良い友だったが、どちらも彫り物を入れていないので不幸だった。[110] 自分たちは友たちほど美しくないと感じていたのである。
ある日、二人は互いに彫り物を入れることにした。一方がもう一方の胸と背に、腕と脚に、そして顔にまで印をつけた。そして終えると、煮炊きの鍋の底から煤を取って、すべての印にすり込んだ。そしてその者は美しく彫られた。
その仕事をした者がもう一方に言った。
「さあ友よ、あなたはたいそう美しくなった。こんどはあなたがわたしに彫ってくれ。」
それから彫られた者は煮炊きの鍋から黒い煤を大きな山ほど削り取り、そしてもう一方が何をされているのか分かる前に、それを頭の先から足の裏まですり込んでしまった。そしてその者はたいそう黒くて脂ぎっていた。煤で覆われた者はたいそう腹を立てて叫んだ。
「わたしはあれほど気をつけてあなたに彫ってやったのに、なぜこんなふうにするのだ。」
二人は戦い始めた。けれども不意に、美しく彫られた者は大きな蜥蜴になって走り去り、高い草のなかに隠れた。一方、煤だらけの者は烏になって村の上を飛び去った。[111]
